utterances.text: I haven't spoken to you in detail about that. It is -- a certain in the border village of Kordun commanded by the Serb, there were a number of Muslims living there quietly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry because in fact that's out of the area we are interested in, that's fine, Mr. Kirudja?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner and Mr. Kirudja, we have only about seven minutes left but I've been reminded to remind you not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once again my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It isn't your fault, Mr. Kirudja, believe you, it's me, the trouble is as I say that I'm not listening through the ear phones.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 9 stories coming from Bihac and the surrounding Bosnia opstinas of Kradusla, Cazin, Bosanski Novi and Bosanska Krupa, thus paint a gloomy picture similar to the one in Sarajevo and Mostar. There are fears that behind the border, the mountains and the forests, unspeakable atrocities may be unfolding. This message is sent in the hope that an alert could be relayed to the authorities with the competence to begin to address the problem before it is too late for the desperate people in the area. Such an action could begin with a relief operation for Bihac and a return of ICRC and UNHCR. You were clearly trying to impress the urgent need for help to these areas. Just very briefly, was there some kind of problem that you were trying to address with this particular report?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA.
utterances.text: Yes. One, both a substance as the report itself says a humanitarian disaster in the making, self-evident as you read out. There was an internal problem in my reporting structure that I was also trying to -- to address, and that is they actually had ordered me to stop telling them about these stories. My own headquarters, arguing that there was no mandate for to us deal with it. And that this activity from our side of the United Nations Protected Area, there was a clear misunderstanding in headquarters that we were spending too much time worrying about this. It was a mistake, and that I didn't want to persist at headquarters. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to move to a major bundle of reports now so I think it's probably better that that's left until Tuesday -- Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Kirudja, I suppose, has been made aware that tomorrow we will not be sitting --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's an UN employee, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. We will be having an UN holiday, on the occasion of the hajj so we will all meet again on Wednesday morning at 9.00, this same courtroom. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else, Mr. Ackerman? I take it you will be providing us with your response on the expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assume you're talking about that major issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I talked to one of your staff people on Friday and said that I would try to get it in this week but you'll recall this morning I said that I was running up against some time problems and I'll do the best I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll get it to you as quickly as I can, Your Honour. It's quite an undertaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour I think if this refers to Mr. Brown, I think more important is for us to know whether we need to call these witnesses so Mr. Brown is not likely to testify until, if Your Honours allow him, I'd say at the earliest after Easter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that could wait, Mr. Ackerman, that could wait another week, and in the meantime you would give priority to what Ms. Korner has just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't know what she means with to know whether we need to call these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Rule 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I mentioned earlier on in private session this morning, the two motions, Donji Vakuf and the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now I know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
